items.title: Expedition 33 Writer Leaves Sandfall to Build a Fund for Story-Led Games
Grand Theft Auto VI Earns Eight The Game Awards 2026 Nominations, but Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s Record of 12 Still Stands
items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominees with eight, but Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is still the record holder.
items.content:
The nominations for Geoff Keighley's The Game Awards 2026 are out, and unsurprisingly, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI leads the pack, having been nominated in eight categories: Game of the Year, Best Action/Adventure, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, and Best Performance (for Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos).

This isn't a record: last year, Sandfall Interactive's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 brought home 12 nominations . It was a prelude to the actual show, where the RPG would win nine prizes (including Game of the Year), setting another record. Before Expedition 33, the record was 11 nominations , shared by Naughty Dog's The Last of Us Part II (2020) and God of War Ragnarök (2022).

However, Grand Theft Auto VI is the first game to be nominated in the Game of the Year category ahead of its release . Such a thing had never happened before: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and Marvel's Deadpool VR were nominated for their respective categories (fighting games and VR games) in 2014 and 2025, but no game had been nominated for GOTY before launch.

GTA VI is also the clear favorite to win the Game of the Year award, especially after the reviews . Still, other games are poised to do well: Remedy's Control Resonant and CAPCOM's Resident Evil Requiem got six each, S-GAME's Phantom Blade Zero got five, while 007 First Light, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Big Walk received four. Scroll down to read the full list of The Game Awards 2026 nominees.

items.title: Lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has left Sandfall Interactive
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, who was responsible for the script of the hit Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is no longer working at Sandfall Interactive. She revealed in an interview with GamesBeat that she left the studio in mid-summer
items.content:
Back to news Lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has left Sandfall Interactive Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, who was responsible for the script of the hit Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, no longer works at Sandfall Interactive. She reported in an interview with GamesBeat that she left the studio in mid-summer.

According to the writer, she resigned after completing all her tasks related to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. What prompted her departure from Sandfall Interactive remains unsaid by Svedberg-Yen, but it likely involves her new ventures.

Currently, Svedberg-Yen wants to focus on her own creative projects, including writing stories for film and television. She also plans to establish a fund to support indie studios developing narrative games. The fund will provide financing at the earliest stages of production. As Svedberg-Yen explained, many teams struggle to find a publisher without a completed demo, but creating one also requires money — through the fund, she hopes to break this barrier and ease the developers' journey.

Svedberg-Yen was one of the first employees at Sandfall Interactive. Initially, she applied for the role of a voice actress but eventually took on scripting for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

items.title: “We’ve parted ways”: Clair Obscur lead writer reveals her next move
items.summary: The lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has revealed that she left Sandfall Interactive in July. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen is now looking beyond the
items.content:
This article needs JavaScript to display. Please turn on JavaScript in your browser and reload the page. The lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has revealed that she left Sandfall Interactive in July. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen is now looking beyond the acclaimed role-playing game, with plans that include supporting other narrative-focused creators.

Asked whether she was still working with the studio, Svedberg-Yen told GamesBeat that she had left after finishing some final work on Expedition 33 . “We’ve parted ways,” she said.

The interview gives fans a clearer picture of what she wants to do next. She discussed both her own stories and an idea for an investment fund that could help smaller teams get narrative-driven games off the ground.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is Sandfall Interactive’s debut game. Image: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive

Her proposed fund would focus on the gap between a creator’s earliest idea and the point at which a publisher can assess a demo. As she explained to GamesBeat, making that demo takes money, but securing funding can itself depend on having something to show.

Svedberg-Yen describes Expedition 33 as a narrative-first game. Image: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive

She also discussed an incubation programme that could help studios think about narrative early in development. Those are ambitions she is working toward; the interview does not announce a launch date for a fund or name games it will finance.

For Svedberg-Yen, story and gameplay need to develop together. She told GamesBeat that some teams approach narrative late in the process, while she sees room for it to influence art, music and gameplay from the beginning.

The game follows an expedition confronting a deadly cycle. Image: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive

Svedberg-Yen said she joined the project in April 2020, when the future studio was still a tiny team. She described Expedition 33 as a narrative-first game from the outset, rather than a story added after its other systems were settled.

The game went on to find a much larger audience than that early team. Its Steam listing describes a role-playing adventure in which an expedition sets out to break a recurring cycle of death.

If the news has made you curious about the game itself, Amazon lists the PS5 edition of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Check the platform on the listing before ordering, as the game is available on other systems too.

Image credit: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 lead writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen confirms Sandfall exit
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead and writer on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has confirmed that she left developer Sandfall Interactive in July.
items.content:
Add us on Image credit: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead and writer on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has confirmed that she left developer Sandfall Interactive in July.

Svedberg-Yen revealed the departure in an interview with GamesBeat published on November 17th. Asked whether she was still working with Sandfall in any way, she said: "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We've parted ways." Sandfall has not commented publicly on her exit.

The interview followed her selection for BAFTA's Breakthrough U.S. programme. Svedberg-Yen said she was "very surprised" by the news, which she first spotted as a calendar invite while sitting in a bagel shop.

Svedberg-Yen, who worked in private equity before joining the game, told GamesBeat she wants to set up a narrative investment fund for story-focused game creators. The aim is to bridge the gap between seed money and publisher deals, since small teams often need a demo to raise money but need money to build a demo. She also described an incubation programme to help studios build story into their games from the start.

"What a lot of studios do is they think of it more like a skin," she said of narrative, adding that some teams bring a writer in late in the hope that story will "make it make sense." Alongside the fund, she is working on two stories of her own, one aimed at TV and one at film, both with game elements.

Expedition 33 was her first game and her first time writing. She joined in April 2020 as the third person on the project, before Sandfall existed as a studio, when its two co-founders were still working at Ubisoft. "It was always, from the very beginning, a narrative-focused game," she said.

The turn-based role-playing game, published by Kepler Interactive, has since collected a long list of awards. That includes Best Narrative among its five wins at the 2026 Game Developers Choice Awards , where it was also named Game of the Year.

items.title: Clair Obscur Expedition 33 gets DLC tease as narrative lead leaves Sandfall
items.content:
Expedition 33's narrative-lead has left Sandfall Interactive, but may have teased fresh DLC content on the way out.

Clair Obscur Expedition 33 was a game you simply couldn’t avoid in 2025, especially with how many awards it gobbled up.

There’ll be no mention of Expedition 33 at this year’s Game Awards however, as when the latest and greatest 2026 games received their nominations yesterday all eyes were on Grand Theft Auto VI .

Still, Expedition 33 is as popular as ever and those who are crossing their fingers more content might be in luck. The game’s narrative lead has alluded to something in the works.

In an interview by Eurogamer news broke that Expedition 33 ’s lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, has left Sandfall Interactive.

The BAFTA award-winner said they parted ways with the studio in July, but not before “wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition.”

When asked what’s next Jennifer said they hope to work on "my own projects, my own stories".

Naturally the interview has us wondering what on earth Sandfall could still be working on with Expedition 33 . The studio has made it clear that the series is meant to be an anthology, so if a new game is ever made it’ll be a new story with new characters.

Story expansions never seemed to be part of the plan, but the game’s narrative-lead’s comments certainly sound like there’s more to come.

There haven’t been any major expansions for Expedition 33 at the time of writing, but one singular, free DLC update was released following the game’s launch.

READ NEXT: 2025 GOTY Drops Free Surprise DLC For First Anniversary

The ‘Thank You Update’ included some new areas to explore, gear to be equipped to the game’s cast, and an endless mode for those who like a challenge. Narratively speaking though it added nothing new to the game.

Obviously we can’t take Jennifer Svedberg-Yen’s words as confirmation a new story is on the way, but we can’t help but speculate.

Speaking from experience, I don’t think Expedition 33 needs any sort of story DLC. Sure, it’d be nice to see, but is there really anywhere else for that story to go?

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's narrative lead wants to change game funding
items.summary: After numerous awards, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen wants to put money on game narratives as a priority in development.
items.content:
After winning numerous awards, Clair Obscur narrative lead Jennifer Svedberg-Yen wants to change the story about priorities in game funding.

The narrative lead behind one of 2025's most critically-acclaimed games , Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, has departed Sandfall after helping catapult Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to notable success as one of the most awarded video games of all time. A few months after leaving the studio, she wants to change the way that narrative design gets funded and advanced in the game industry.

In a profile piece with GamesBeat , Svedberg-Yen describes a personal goal of reshaping how the industry develops stories and what it does to support, or not support, the creative talent that keeps it aloft. After leaving Sandfall back in July, Svedberg-Yen—who previously worked in finance and private equity—wants to put game narratives first and reverse the common wisdom that treats it as an afterthought during development.

"A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin," Svedberg-Yen told Gamesbeat. "They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense. But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other." Svedberg-Yen has set up a fund dedicated to advancing the art of narrative design and create new funding models focused on curating and nurturing talent.

Related: What Rami Ismail learned during his return to game development

"I’m not trying to compete with publishers," Svedberg-Yen explains. "But I’m trying to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make."

Sverberg-Yen has not yet detailed exactly how the fund will work, but emphasizes that it's one of her main focuses in 2027, alongside her own projects.

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry," she says."

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer has ‘parted ways’ with Sandfall
items.summary: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur…
items.content:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur

Video Game News 18th Nov 2026 / 4:54 pm Posted by Rhiannon Bevan Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead narrative designer has left Sandfall Interactive.

After winning a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her work on the game, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen confirmed that she left Sandfall in July of this year.

As reported by GamesBeat , Svedberg-Yen did not go into detail about her departure: “I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We’ve parted ways.”

She added that she wants to work on her “own projects”, while helping to mentor up-and-coming writers.

“The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help,” Svedberg-Yen said. “That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.”

She also advocated for better working conditions for the creatives who make games. “I don’t believe in starving artists,” she said. “We should pay our people properly so everyone can have health care, have vacations.”

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 [77 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/clair-obscur-expedition-33/ >Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was a hit with players and critics alike when it launched in 2025. It went on to be an awards show darling, scooping up Game of the Year awards, including the much-sought-after GOTY at The Game Awards [527 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/events/the-game-awards/ >The Game Awards that year. In fact, it was the most nominated game in The Game Awards history , an accolade that hasn’t even been taken by Grand Theft Auto 6 [283 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/grand-theft-auto-6/ >Grand Theft Auto 6 , which leads in nominations this year .

Svedberg-Yen’s work was widely acclaimed, as many praised the game’s writing. Despite this, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was her first writing credit on a game. It remains to be seen if she works with another studio now that she has left Sandfall.

As for Sandfall, the studio is yet to reveal its next project following on from Clair Obscur’s success. It remains the studio’s only game release.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s Narrative Lead Left Sandfall Interactive in July
items.summary: Following her win of the BAFTA Breakthrough US award, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen said that she wrapped up "some final stuff for Expedition."
items.content:
Following her win of the BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her work on 2025’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the lead narrative designer on the RPG, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, has revealed that she is no longer working at studio Sandfall Interactive. Speaking to GamesBeat , she confirmed that she left the studio all the way back in July, and alluded to a bit of content that might be making its way to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

“No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition ,” she said when asked if she was still working at Sandfall Interactive. “We’ve parted ways.” When asked about why she decided to leave, she offered little in the way of details aside from noting that she wanted to work on “my own projects, my own stories”. This work also involves working to establish a fund that could mentor new and upcoming narrative designers in the games industry.

She spoke about this fund and how her background in finance helps her play a role in establishing it. As for why she was doing it, she said that in its current state, the games industry has trouble figuring out how to integrate narrative elements into the pipeline for a typical game’s development. Along with mentoring those new to the industry, the fund would also be an “incubation program” to help development teams make these integrations.

“One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers. This is the chicken-and-egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers, you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money, you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.”

“I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.”

She also spoke about how times have been quite tough for the games industry, and that ultimately, “The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help.”

“That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.”

As for Svedberg-Yen’s last bit of work with Sandfall, the studio hasn’t really announced any major new content for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 yet. However, studio CEO Guillaume Broche has said that the team is going to “go a bit crazy” with its next major project .

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's Lead Writer Has Left Sandfall to Help Game Devs Tell Better Stories
items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset.
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead for Expedition 33, won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award earlier this year, and she’s since been consulting on stories across the industry.

Expedition 33 was her first video game (she came from a career in private equity), but it won more than 400 awards and received almost universal critical acclaim, in part due to its blend of real-time and traditional turn-based RPG mechanics, and partly because of its mysterious story, strong emotional beats, and brilliant characters.

Svedberg-Yen is now setting up a fund with the aim of advancing narrative design in video games and nurturing new writing talent.

“I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge,” Svedberg-Yen told GamesBeat . “We’re making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There’s so much disruption in the industry right now.”

Outside of the constant layoffs and upheaval in the industry, there’s also a sense, still, that narrative isn’t as respected as other parts of game design.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense.

“But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

The award-winning writer believes this approach limits what games can achieve. Expedition 33 was designed with a narrative-first approach, with the game systems built around the story to reinforce the themes and pace the big moments out.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game. I think that’s why we were able to achieve the results that we did in terms of integrating all the different pieces into a wonderful collaborative whole. There was that consistency from the very beginning.”

According to Svedberg-Yen, she’s received messages from players about how Expedition 33 helped them deal with grief and navigate the world after suffering a personal loss.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t seem like we’ll see more of Svedberg-Yen’s work in video games any time soon. Outside of the fund, she has a couple of ideas for TV, but she left Sandfall in July “after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition.”

Following success at pretty much every major video game award show (most recently including scooping up Best Game at the BAFTA Awards ), Sandfall Interactive is now busy planning its next project. Details of that currently remain under wraps, though the suggestion is that it will be another adventure set in the same Clair Obscur universe .

"Wearing its inspirations on its sleeve, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 paints itself into the pantheon of great RPGs with a brilliant combat system and a gripping, harrowing story," IGN wrote in our Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 review , dubbing it a "modern RPG classic."

items.title: It's Official: Clair Obscur Will Never Be The Same
items.summary: It's officially the end of an era for the Clair Obscur franchise, and its future is now uncertain.
items.content:
Lune holding a glowing object while looking surprised in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Nicholas Becher Published Nov 17, 2026, 9:33 PM EST Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There's been a major development behind the scenes at Sandfall Interactive, the studio behind the award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , and the future of the franchise will officially never be the same. Sandfall Interactive and the idea behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 started from extremely humble beginnings. Before there was even a proper studio, two Ubisoft developers and a writer were already shaping what would eventually become one of gaming's biggest breakout hits.

Their ambitious vision for a story-driven RPG gradually evolved into a global phenomenon, with Expedition 33 earning hundreds of awards including GOTY and widespread acclaim for its memorable characters, heartbreaking story, and innovative gameplay. That extraordinary success has raised expectations for a Clair Obscur sequel or follow-up project through the roof.

However, in a new interview with Games Beat , lead writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has officially confirmed her departure from Sandfall Interactive, marking a major turning point for the franchise.

In a November 17 interview with Dean Takahashi, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she departed Sandfall Interactive back in July 2026, several months before the news became public. When asked whether she was still involved with the studio in any capacity, the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 lead writer gave a very blunt answer:

"I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. We’ve parted ways."

The announcement came during a much broader conversation about Svedberg-Yen's future, following her selection for BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. recognition. She explained that she's working to establish a narrative investment fund designed to help smaller game developers secure early funding, while encouraging studios to prioritize storytelling throughout the development process.

That philosophy played an enormous role in Expedition 33 's creation. Svedberg-Yen was involved before Sandfall had even formally been established, joining two Ubisoft developers in April 2020 as the team's third member. She helped develop the game's original premise and themes, explaining that "Narrative is king" was an important part of the studio's approach from the beginning.

Close window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-44955267"] = '" Close "'; Looking back, she spoke highly of the collaboration between Sandfall's various creative departments and said she was especially proud of how strongly the characters connected with players. The way fans responded to the game's themes of grief, and the personal conversations it inspired, had an impact she never anticipated.

Beyond her planned investment fund, Svedberg-Yen also revealed that she's developing two personal storytelling projects, one intended for television and another for film, both incorporating gaming elements. She also emphasized that her biggest priority is helping the gaming industry support its creative talent, particularly younger developers struggling to break into the business.

While she didn't provide a detailed explanation for her departure or suggest that the split was acrimonious, it's undoubtedly a significant loss for Sandfall. With its original narrative lead no longer at the studio, any future Clair Obscur installment will have to move forward without one of the key creative minds who helped define Expedition 33 's award-winning storytelling.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Patch v1.5.6 is now live!
items.summary: Expeditioners, Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic! Content New supported language (text): Arabic [/*] Credi
items.content:
Expeditioners,

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!

Content

  • New supported language (text): Arabic

    [/*]

  • Credits updated (new linguists, testers and fonts)

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where applying burn after an enemy has been stunned causes them to be able to act immediately after recovering from the stun.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Cleim weapon level 10 Lumina effect that does not trigger correctly on every instance of area of effect skills.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Martenon’s Lumina effects that do not work if Sciel does not have two consecutive turns.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Sireso weapon, Level 4 Lumina, and Powerful buff, from Pictos/Luminas, applied at the start of battle may override each other depending on the character's position in combat.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Chromatic Lampmaster's AOE skill missing a sound cue on the jump attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Sirene's Widow Ballet missing SFX during second charm attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed characters in combat that may have displaced heads in Photo Mode if they were not seen while turning on Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Various minor fixes of the UI and localizations.

    [/*]

We are aware of a crash affecting some of you when loading into the Reacher or going out of the Manor. This crash is related to some specific PC configurations. Until we fix this issue, you can work around it by setting ‘Global Illumination’ to anything below ‘Epic’ temporarily.

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Dispatch Bundle
items.summary: Expeditioners! Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Dispatch are now available together in a 10% off bundle! Bundle art by Derek Stratton This is a really special bundle for us - since its release, Dispatch left such an impact on us and immediat
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Dispatch are now available together in a 10% off bundle! 

Bundle art by Derek Stratton

This is a really special bundle for us - since its release, Dispatch left such an impact on us and immediately became one of our favourites.   

Our games are quite different, but we couldn’t help ourselves - and ultimately, we just want more people to discover the powerful stories and artistry behind these games.   

So in the words of our Creative Director, Guillaume Broche: “Play Dispatch, it’s very very cool”

Save 10% off both games by purchasing this bundle!

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Happy 1 Year Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33!! The details of this patch are written out below:

New content

  • Added 1st Anniversary haircuts for the expedition!

    • Gustave's Anniversary haircut is available at the Gestral Merchant near Stone Wave Cliffs.

      [/*]

    • Verso + Maelle + Lune + Sciel + Monoco's Anniversary haircuts are available at the Gestral Merchant near Grosse Tête on the World Map.

      [/*]
    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where Danseuse outfit for Lune and Sciel made the character menu too obscur.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where it was not possible to open a rest point in various locations when an in-world dialogue was playing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed collision issues in various locations.

    [/*]

  • Adjusted some achievement text for consistency.

    • We've noticed something went wrong after adjusting this, we're investigating now to resolve the issue

      [/*]

    • Fixed the issue! We've readjusted some of the achievement descriptions back to the correct achievements. Thank you for your patience!!

      [/*]
    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - and most importantly, thank you for all of your support this entire year!! We wish you a wonderful anniversary day and hope you enjoy some cake to celebrate with us!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
